verdict.label: Worth checking
verdict.headline: Rey Cortiço Lunch
verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: Tomorrow (TOMORROW) I’d go with a lunch check for Rey Cortiço, but it’s a bit of a rare window. With the wind looking cross-on and the spot not syncing perfectly, I’m not trusting it until I see it on the Surfline and MEO Beachcam first—if it looks rough or chopped, I’ll skip. The tide being at dead low could still line up the sandbanks for something workable, but it’s very much a “cams decide” call. Check the cams first and only leave if it’s clearly cleaner than expected.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Medium confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 22 kJ, 9 s period, lully 1/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
